Part 1 · APIs

How software talks to software.

Before AI can use your apps, it has to be able to ask them for things.

01 Apps asking apps

Your apps are always asking other apps.

Your weather app doesn’t own a single thermometer. It asks a service that does.

Press a service to send it a question.

05 Your key

An API key is your membership card.

A service gives each customer a key, and checks it on every order.

Keep it secret. Whoever holds it orders on your tab.

Example
Or press the card itself.

There’s no master key.

07 Some keys need more care

Some keys need more care.

A key that only looks at public things is low risk. A key that can spend money, reach private things or act in your name is high risk. Sort six example keys.

      08 Rate limits

      Order too often and the counter closes.

      A service’s ordering counter only takes so many orders a minute Rate limit. Go over, and it says ‘try later’.

        The universal plug for AI.

        09 One socket per app

        Every app has its own socket.

        Your AI reaches each app through an adapter made only for that app.

        Like travelling overseas with a bag of plugs, one for every country.

        11 One plug for all

        MCP gives every app the same plug.

        The universal plug

        MCP

        MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. You can forget the name.

        A service builds one MCP adapter, and any AI that speaks MCP can plug in.

        For illustration

        Before: four apps, four different adapters.

        12 The big idea

        Think of MCP as USB-C for AI.

        Before USB-C, every gadget had its own charger. Now one plug fits nearly everything.

        Not connected

        The comparison Anthropic, MCP’s creator, uses itself.

        MCP sits on top of the API. It doesn’t replace it.

        14 Two kinds of job

        Look things up, or take action.

        Some jobs only look. Others change things. You choose which the AI may do.

        Look things up

        Read

        Looking only. Nothing is changed.

        • Find a documentSearches your files and shows the result.
        • Check your calendarLooks at your events. Changes nothing.
        • Pull official statisticsFetches official figures and the source.

        Take action

        Write

        Locked

        • Book a meetingAdds an event to your calendar.
        • Draft an email for you to checkWrites it. You read it and press send.
        • Make a designCreates a design from your request.

        Only if you allow it, one step at a time.

        16 Signing in safely

        You sign in. The AI never sees your password.

        It’s like a hotel key card: it opens only the rooms you agreed to.

        A firm rule

        If an AI ever asks for your username and password, the answer is no.

        Example
        Calendar Connected

        Nothing is connected yet. Press Connect to begin.

        Your question Question: What’s the unemployment rate in Victoria? Example

        Web search

        Reads whatever comes up first.

        Source
        Often unclear
        Date

        The MCP connection answer appears here.

        MCP connection

        Goes straight to official figures.

        Source
        Data Commons, a free Google service that gathers official figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), World Bank, UN and others. datacommons.org (opens in a new tab)
        Date
        Shown with the figure

        The point isn’t that the AI is smarter. It’s that you can check where the answer came from.

        18 An open standard

        MCP no longer belongs to one company.

        A shared industry standard, like USB. That’s why most AI tools now support it.

        1. Anthropic, the company behind Claude, releases MCP as an open standard.

        2. OpenAI and Google add support in their own AI tools.

        3. Anthropic hands MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation, part of the Linux Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, OpenAI and Block.

        Press a date to highlight it. Press it again to clear.

        Staying safe

        A little care goes a long way.

        Two ways to stay in control of what an AI does.

        19 The risky combination

        Never give an AI all three at once.

        What this means

        Turn on the switches to see what an AI can do.

        For illustration

        A web page or email can hide instructions aimed at your AI. If it can also see your data and send things out, it could leak them.

        Known asPrompt injection

        Idea: Simon Willison, ‘the lethal trifecta’

                21 To take home

                Three words to take home.

                • API

                  the ordering counter

                • MCP

                  the universal plug

                • Connector

                  the button you press

                Three habits

                1. 1Start with read-only connections (they can look, not change).
                2. 2Stick to well-known companies’ connectors.
                3. 3If a connection doesn’t show up, start a new chat or restart the app.
